title: Lorazepam — Pediatric Status Epilepticus
sources: Drug_Dosing_Peds_Weight_Based_Spec.md (cross-checked vs Stanford & Riley Children's pathways)

changelog.change: Updated buildNote to cross-link the newly-built second-line set (peds-fosphenytoin-status, peds-levetiracetam-status, peds-valproate-status) and clarify neonatal phenobarbital lives in the separate neonatal-seizures module.

purpose: First-line IV benzodiazepine for pediatric status epilepticus when IV access is available.

rule.repeat: May repeat once after 5 minutes if the seizure persists

doses.notes: If no IV access: IM/IN midazolam is the preferred first agent — see the midazolam card.

buildNote: First-line benzodiazepine sibling of peds-midazolam-status. If seizures persist after an adequate benzodiazepine dose, the second-line set is peds-fosphenytoin-status, peds-levetiracetam-status, and peds-valproate-status (ESETT 2019 — roughly equivalent efficacy, pick by contraindication profile). Phenobarbital for neonatal seizures is a different population/algorithm, covered in the neonatal-seizures reference module. Diazepam rectal (Diastat) as an out-of-hospital/no-access option is not yet built.
